rows.text: Most spellslinger decks want cheap spells. This one wants EXPENSIVE ones — Y'shtola only triggers on noncreature spells of mana value three or more, and every trigger is two damage to each opponent and two life to you. Her draw clause then checks whether a player lost four or more life this turn, which means the deck's real rhythm is two big spells per turn, every turn. One trigger is damage. Two is damage and a card.

rows.name: Y'shtola, Night's Blessed
rows.text: vigilance on a 2/4, two damage to each opponent and two life to you per noncreature spell of mana value three or more, and a card at end step if anybody lost four or more life this turn.

Count to two. A single trigger drains each opponent for two, which is not four — so it does not draw. Two triggers in the same turn does. Sequencing two mid-cost spells into one turn is worth more than spreading them over two.

rows.name: Lyse Hext
rows.text: noncreature spells cost {1} less, she grows on each one, and she gains double strike once you have cast two in a turn. She is the enabler and a clock at the same time.

rows.name: Alisaie Leveilleur
rows.text: the SECOND spell each turn costs {2} less, which is exactly the turn pattern Y'shtola is asking for.

rows.name: Alphinaud Leveilleur
rows.text: a card whenever you cast your second spell each turn. He and Alisaie fetch each other, so drawing either finds the pair.

rows.name: Papalymo Totolymo
rows.text: one damage to each opponent and one life to you on EVERY noncreature spell, with no mana value floor. He fills the gap Y'shtola leaves on cheap spells, and he sacrifices to strip the table's biggest creatures.

rows.name: Professor Onyx
rows.text: two drain and two gain on every instant and sorcery you cast or copy.

rows.name: Sedgemoor Witch
rows.text: a Pest for every instant and sorcery, on a menacing warded body.

rows.name: Circle of Power
rows.text: two cards, and a Wizard token that pings each opponent on every noncreature spell.

rows.name: Sanguine Bond
rows.text: every point of life you gain becomes a point an opponent loses. Y'shtola alone is gaining you two a trigger, so this roughly doubles the deck's clock.

rows.name: Rosa, Resolute White Mage
rows.text: a counter and lifelink each combat, which with Sanguine Bond turns an attack into a drain.

rows.name: Kaya, Intangible Slayer
rows.text: hexproof, so she sticks, and the plus is three drained and three gained every turn.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: their turns pay for your expensive turns.

rows.name: Decorum Dissertation
rows.text: two cards and two life loss, and paradigm makes it recur FREE at the beginning of every one of your main phases for the rest of the game.

rows.name: Dig Through Time
rows.text: delve is easy in a deck casting this many spells.

rows.name: Frantic Search
rows.text: free, and it untaps three lands so the second big spell of the turn is castable.

rows.name: Cryptic Command
rows.text: four mana, two modes, and it is a Y'shtola trigger.

rows.name: Krile Baldesion
rows.text: returns a creature from your graveyard matching each noncreature spell's mana value.

rows.name: Quistis Trepe
rows.text: recasts an instant or sorcery out of ANY graveyard on arrival.

rows.name: Curiosity
rows.text: on Y'shtola, her own damage trigger draws you a card each time.

rows.name: Ophidian Eye
rows.text: the same with flash.

rows.name: Grim Tutor
rows.text: any card in the deck.

rows.name: Beseech the Mirror
rows.text: bargain it and cast the tutored card free if it costs four or less.

guide.title: Interaction, all of it Y'shtola triggers

rows.text: Every counterspell here costs three or more on purpose. They answer a threat AND drain the table.

rows.name: Dovin's Veto
rows.text: uncounterable, two mana — the one exception, and worth it.

rows.name: Fierce Guardianship
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free, pointed at a creature.

rows.name: Mana Sculpt
rows.text: counter, and with a Wizard out it refunds you their mana.

rows.name: Rewind
rows.text: counter and untap four lands, so it is effectively free on your own turn.

rows.name: Anguished Unmaking
rows.text: instant-speed exile for any nonland permanent.

rows.name: Dismember
rows.text: one mana and four life, or three mana.

rows.name: Avatar's Wrath
rows.text: exiles the board while leaving one of yours, and locks opponents to casting from hand until your next turn.

rows.name: Elspeth, Sun's Champion
rows.text: three bodies a turn, or a one-sided wrath against the big creatures this deck cannot block.

rows.name: Inkshield
rows.text: prevents a lethal alpha strike and turns it into a flying army.

rows.name: Perch Protection
rows.text: four fliers, or gifted, a full phase-out with your life locked — the answer to a combo kill.

rows.name: Lulu, Stern Guardian
rows.text: stun counters on whatever attacks you, and a proliferate outlet to make them stick.

rows.name: Jill, Shiva's Dominant
rows.text: bounces a permanent on entry, and flips into a Saga that taps every opponent's lands.

rows.name: Approach of the Second Sun
rows.text: seven mana, gain seven, then cast it again seven cards later and win outright. In a deck that stalls the board and draws this much, it is the cleanest kill available.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: your life total climbs fast between Y'shtola, Papalymo and Rosa. Fifty life to any target ends a game with no combat and no targeting restrictions.

rows.name: Sanguine Bond
rows.text: with the Reservoir and the drain triggers, the table's life total falls on its own.

rows.name: Multiversal Recruitment
rows.text: a nonlegendary copy of Y'shtola or Sedgemoor Witch, twice with flashback.

rows.name: Coalition Relic
rows.text: fixes all three colours and stores a mana for the second big spell.

rows.name: Relic of Legends
rows.text: taps any legendary creature for mana, and this deck is full of them.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for exactly what you need.

rows.name: Arcane Signet
rows.text: the same.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep mana and a cost reducer. Lyse Hext or Alisaie Leveilleur is what turns "one big spell a turn" into "two big spells a turn", and two is the number that makes Y'shtola draw.

Hold interaction until your own turn when you safely can. A counterspell cast on your turn is a Y'shtola trigger and a step toward the second one; the same card cast on their turn is just a counterspell.

rows.name: Y'shtola, Night's Blessed
rows.text: four mana and a 2/4 with vigilance, so she blocks well and survives most sweepers aimed at bigger boards. She is worth recasting after removal — the triggers are the deck.

rows.name: Approach of the Second Sun
rows.text: start it once the board is stable and you can protect the second cast. Both copies must be cast FROM YOUR HAND, so Beseech the Mirror's free-cast mode does not finish it.
